# 1 Clement Chapter 26 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 26 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_026_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 26

**26:1** Shall we then consider it a great and wonderful thing if the Creator of all things should raise up those who have served him in holiness and in the assurance of good faith, when even through a bird he demonstrates to us the greatness of his promise?

**26:2** For it says somewhere: "You shall raise me up and I will give you thanks;" and: "I lay down and slept, and I arose, for you are with me."

**26:3** And again Job says: "And you shall raise up this flesh of mine, which has endured all these things."

---

*LOGOS preserves the rhetorical question form of v. 1, which is the rhetorical climax of the phoenix argument. The "somewhere" citation formula (*pou*) is characteristic of early Christian use of the Psalms.*
